resolved_by: Supreme Court's decision in Snyder v. United States, 603 U.S. 1 (2024), which resolved the circuit split and held that 18 U.S.C. § 666 reaches only quid pro quo bribery, not gratuities
issue: Does 18 U.S.C. § 666 criminalize gratuities paid to or received by state or local officials, or only quid pro quo bribery?

sides.position: Section 666 reaches illegal gratuities as well as quid pro quo bribery (the pre-Snyder rule of this circuit)
cases: United States v. McClain, Nos. 25-2349 & 25-2350 (7th Cir. 2026) (describing the prior precedent)

sides.position: Section 666 reaches only quid pro quo bribery, not gratuities (the rule adopted in Snyder)
cases: United States v. McClain, Nos. 25-2349 & 25-2350 (7th Cir. 2026)

this_court: applies Snyder: § 666 reaches only quid pro quo bribery, so the pre-Snyder jury instructions on gratuities were error
quote: In Snyder, the Court resolved a circuit split and overturned our precedent that § 666 criminalized illegal gratuities as well as quid pro quo bribery, ruling that § 666 only punished quid pro quo bribery.
cite: United States v. Michael McClain, No. 25-2350 (7th Cir. 2026)
